description: Notion workspace access via Notion's official hosted MCP server: search, read, create and update pages, databases and comments. Each user authorizes their own Notion account; on first use, start the authorization flow to get a consent link where the user picks the workspace and pages to share.

notion-create-pages.description: Creates one or more Notion pages with the given properties and content; all pages of one call share the parent. Parent: "page_id" for a regular page, "data_source_id" for a database item (fetch the database first to get its collection:// data source URL and schema — never pass a database URL as page_id). With no destination named, pass "creation_mode": "draft" (a private workspace-level page; tell the user it is a draft and offer to move it). Content is Notion-flavored Markdown without the title (the title goes into properties); for anything beyond plain headings/lists/links, read the spec first by fetching the id `notion://docs/enhanced-markdown-spec` with notion-fetch. Properties are a JSON map of property names to values, using the exact names from the fetched data source schema; every data source has exactly one title property (not always named "title"); pages outside a database take only "title". Value formats: dates split into "date:{property}:start" / ":end" / ":is_datetime" (0|1); numbers as numbers; checkboxes "__YES__" / "__NO__"; relations as arrays of page URLs or IDs; properties named "id" or "url" are prefixed "userDefined:". Optional "template_id" pre-populates a database item (omit content then; it fills in asynchronously). Optional "icon" (emoji or image URL) and "cover" (image URL).

notion-update-page.description: Updates one Notion page — its properties, content, icon/cover — by page_id and command. Commands: "update_properties" (properties map, omitted properties unchanged); "update_content" (targeted edit: the smallest exact old_str from the fetched page that identifies the target, and new_str); "insert_content" (prepend/append); "replace_content" (whole page — prefer a targeted command; it fails if child pages/databases would be lost, which requires allow_deleting_content — ask the user first, never assume); "apply_template". Fetch the page before editing unless it is already loaded, match its heading levels, block types and style, and make the smallest complete edit. Content is Notion-flavored Markdown; for anything beyond plain headings/lists/links, read the spec first by fetching the id `notion://docs/enhanced-markdown-spec` with notion-fetch. Property value formats: exact names from the fetched data source schema; dates split into "date:{property}:start" / ":end" / ":is_datetime" (0|1); numbers as numbers; checkboxes "__YES__" / "__NO__"; relations as arrays of page URLs or IDs; properties named "id" or "url" are prefixed "userDefined:"; pages outside a database take only "title". Leave "allow_async" unset or false so the call returns the finished result; an "async_task" response means the update is still being applied — re-fetch the page shortly before depending on it.
